questions.stem: Which AWS service is the native Infrastructure-as-Code tool?
questions.explanation: CloudFormation is AWS's declarative IaC service; templates in YAML/JSON describe resources to provision.

questions.stem: CloudFormation is best described as which paradigm?
questions.explanation: CFN describes the desired end state; AWS computes how to reach it.

questions.stem: Before applying changes, CloudFormation can show what will change via:
questions.explanation: A change set previews additions, removals, and replacements before execution.

questions.stem: Terraform's equivalent of a CFN change set is:
questions.explanation: `terraform plan` generates an execution plan describing actions to add/change/destroy.

questions.stem: Which CloudFormation feature deploys the same stack to multiple accounts and Regions?
questions.explanation: StackSets propagate a single template to many accounts/Regions, often used for landing-zone guard rails.

questions.stem: Which CFN intrinsic returns a logical reference (often the primary identifier of a resource)?
questions.explanation: `!Ref` resolves to the resource's primary identifier (e.g. bucket name, instance id, parameter value).

questions.stem: Which intrinsic substitutes variables into a string with ${} syntax?
questions.explanation: `!Sub` performs variable substitution like `!Sub "arn:aws:s3:::${BucketName}"`.

questions.stem: Idempotency in IaC means:
choices: Re-applying the same template with the same inputs produces no further changes
Resources can only be created once
Templates run only once per Region
questions.explanation: Declarative IaC converges to the desired state; if state already matches, apply is a no-op — that's idempotency.

questions.stem: CFN 'drift detection' is used to:
choices: Compare actual resource state to the template and flag manual changes
questions.explanation: Drift detection surfaces changes made outside CloudFormation (e.g. console clicks) so they can be remediated.

questions.stem: If a CFN stack creation fails partway, the default behaviour is:
choices: Roll back, deleting any resources already created
questions.explanation: On failure, CFN rolls back the stack by default; you can disable rollback for debugging.

questions.stem: Which CFN section is mandatory in every template?
questions.explanation: Only the Resources section is required; the others are optional.

questions.stem: Terraform state is typically stored in:
choices: An S3 backend with DynamoDB for state locking (a common pattern)
questions.explanation: Production Terraform uses a remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB lock table for AWS) so teams share state safely.

questions.stem: Which is true of CloudFormation vs Terraform?
choices: CFN is multi-cloud; Terraform is AWS-only
Terraform is multi-cloud via providers; CFN is AWS-only
questions.explanation: Terraform spans cloud providers via its provider plugin system; CFN is AWS-specific.

questions.stem: AWS CDK lets you write infra in languages like TypeScript and synthesise to:
questions.explanation: CDK synthesises CFN templates from typed code, gaining language abstractions while reusing CFN's engine.

questions.stem: AWS SAM is best described as:
choices: A CFN extension that simplifies serverless app templates
questions.explanation: SAM extends CFN with shorthand transforms for Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and a local CLI for invoking functions.

questions.stem: Why prefer CloudFormation YAML over JSON?
choices: YAML supports comments and is easier to read
questions.explanation: Both are valid, but YAML supports comments and anchors and is generally more readable for humans.

questions.stem: Which CFN property prevents a resource from being deleted when the stack is deleted?
questions.explanation: `DeletionPolicy: Retain` keeps the resource (e.g. S3 bucket or RDS) when the stack is deleted — preventing accidental data loss.

questions.stem: Cross-stack referencing in CFN is achieved via:
questions.explanation: One stack exports an Output; another imports via !ImportValue. Use sparingly because exports lock stacks together.

questions.stem: Which IaC pattern lets you parameterise an environment so the same template can deploy dev, staging, prod?
choices: Separate templates per env with duplication
questions.explanation: Parameters (plus Mappings/Conditions) let one template deploy multiple environments without code duplication.

questions.stem: A 'replace' update in CFN happens when:
choices: A property change requires the underlying resource to be recreated (e.g. DBInstanceIdentifier)
questions.explanation: Some property changes can't be done in place; CFN creates a new resource and deletes the old — watch for data loss.

questions.stem: Which Terraform command initialises providers and the backend?
questions.explanation: `terraform init` downloads providers and configures the backend (state).

questions.stem: Which best motivates Infrastructure as Code?
questions.explanation: IaC makes infrastructure repeatable, peer-reviewable, and recoverable — the same benefits as application code in version control.

questions.stem: An AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<String> parameter in CFN pulls its value from:
choices: SSM Parameter Store at stack deploy time
questions.explanation: Such parameters resolve to the live SSM Parameter Store value when the stack is created/updated.

questions.stem: Which approach is MOST aligned with 'cattle, not pets'?
choices: SSHing in to manually patch a long-lived server
Treating servers as immutable: deploy a new AMI rather than mutate the running one
questions.explanation: Immutable infrastructure (replace, don't mutate) underpins reproducibility and rollback — the cattle mindset.

questions.stem: Which CFN feature provides modular templates inside a larger stack?
questions.explanation: Nested stacks let you compose a parent template from child stacks, each a separate template file.
